paper.title: Stylometric and Topic Analysis of a Historical Text. A Computerized Study of General Averescu's 'War Memoirs' (1916-1918)
paper.abstract: The study applies stylometric tools to analyze the relationship between topic and style in a WWI work, General Averescu's War Memoirs. New stylometric indices are suggested and applied.

artifact_assessment.evidence: The analysed text is a named published source, "[2] AVERESCU A., Notiţe Zilnice Din Războiu (1916-1918), Editura 'Cultura Naională Bucureşti', 1935", and the authors link supporting material: "[16] TEODORESCU H.N., BOLEA C., Tiny dictionary of words and expressions in Romanian used during the WWI period ... http://iit.academiaromana-is.ro/centenar/dict en.html". No code is linked.

verdict.summary: Empirical stylometric study of a single historical text using descriptive statistics and a few simple ratio indices; formalism is proportionate, self-citation is mildly elevated, and some statistical results are misinterpreted.

papers.provenance:
## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** Stylometric, topic and pronoun-frequency analysis of three sections of a 1935 WWI memoir, with a few proposed ratio indices (personalization, negation, verbal/nominal color).
**Level:** 2 (Low)
**Rationale:** The work applies standard corpus statistics (Zipf fits, hapax/dis-legomena, Sichel and Honore measures, chi-square, correlation) to one text. The new indices are simple count ratios. No new algorithm or model.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 0 numbered (inline ratio definitions: Ip, Ineg, Ivc, Inc, Ic)
- Theorems: 0
- Proofs: 0
- Equations: about 7 (ratio indices, Sichel and Honore measures, regression lines)

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 0
Expected range (Level 2): 0-15
Ratio: 0x upper bound

**Assessment:** Proportionate. Each equation is a count ratio or a standard stylometric measure that defines exactly what is computed; none dresses a list operation in set notation. The braces around the list of top words are a plain listing, not set algebra.

### Issues
No formalism theater. Statistical interpretation is weak in places: a chi-square p-value of 0.893 is read as "a significant chance to be different", and p = 0.466 as "doubt that the two populations are identical"; the "artifice" of dividing counts by ten to make chi-square non-significant is not a valid procedure. The negation index is typeset inconsistently (Ineq/Ineg) and the nominal color index formula has lost its division sign.

---

## Citation Analysis

Four of 24 references are by the first author (Teodorescu): [1] the companion polarity/sentiment paper on the same text, [3] a sentiment analysis of medical transplant literature, [15] supporting material for [1], and [16] the authors' dictionary of period words. SCR about 17%, in the elevated 15-20% band. All four are methodologically or directly related to the present work; none is irrelevant. Several references are self-hosted web pages rather than peer-reviewed works.

---

## Structural Analysis

Claims are generally tied to reported counts and test statistics, though some conclusions (the memoir as "apologia", "self-praise") go beyond what pronoun counts can show. Limitations are acknowledged inline ("much more extensive studies should be conducted", the partition result is "a preliminary conclusion"). The underlying text is a named published book and the authors link their supporting dictionary and annexes; no code (the Visual C counting program) is released.

---

## Conclusion

A descriptive digital-humanities study with formalism appropriate to its level. Its main weaknesses are statistical: several p-values are misread, and a rescaling trick is used to change test outcomes. Self-citation is mildly elevated but relevant.

paper.title: IT Driven Distributed Consensus for an Integrated Globalized World
paper.abstract: The blockchain technology, BCT, will provide one of the main web-tool of the future, featured with what will be the true peer-to-peer relation, free of the third part, dysfunctional and problem maker term. In the same time, Artificial Intelligence, comes out from the last AI winter with an irrepressible openness for socially requested applications. Both, are ready to support dramatic changes in how our complex and dynamic world is governed. The decision mechanism, at any level in our society, can be improved by the use of the last information technologies, ITs. The main malfunctions of our world are reviewed in order to correlate them with the possible solutions provided by the emergent ITs. The BCT is presented and its use in the making decision process investigated. The impact on the foreseen iDemocracy, iConsensus and iGovernance is evaluated.

artifact_assessment.evidence: no availability statement or link in the text; the voting scheme is described only on paper and nothing was implemented

flag_details.FORMALISM_THEATER: Level 1 position essay wraps simple bookkeeping in notation: a decision is written as the list-of-lists D = ((A1), ..., (Am)) of texts, wallets as VWi = 1 and OWj = 0 for index ranges, and the competence weighting as matrices R(D), R'(D) with Greek-letter ratios gamma(D) and delta(D). All of this is a weighted vote tally expressible in a few sentences, and the notation is internally inconsistent (Ck uses R(D) rather than the normalized R'(D); V0 is computed from O+).
flag_details.UNSUPPORTED_CLAIMS: The bulk of the paper consists of sweeping assertions without evidence or citation, e.g. that politicians are "generally low level performers from media or from the law system", that NGOs offer "no hope", and that AI-based administration "will reduce the current dysfunctional bureaucratic practices". Cited support is largely popular Kindle books and web articles; no evaluation of the proposed scheme is given.

verdict.summary: Socio-political position essay proposing a blockchain-based weighted voting scheme; the scheme is notated with decorative matrices and lists for a simple weighted tally, and the argument rests on unsupported assertions.

## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** Essay on the failings of representative democracy and a sketched blockchain voting scheme (voteCoins sent to option wallets; competence-weighted votes; iterative re-voting).
**Level:** 1 (Trivial)
**Rationale:** No algorithm, protocol, proof or implementation is contributed. The voting scheme is a weighted tally layered on existing cryptocurrency transactions, described at the level of a concept proposal.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 0 numbered
- Theorems: 0
- Proofs: 0
- Equations: about 15 (wallet initialisation, list-of-lists D, competence arrays, matrices R(D), R'(D), Omega(D), indices gamma and delta)

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 0
Expected range (Level 1): 0-5
Ratio: 0x upper bound

**Assessment:** Necessity test fails. Every formal element could be replaced by a sentence ("each voter's vote on an article is weighted by how well their competences match the article's requirements, and the weighted yes/no/abstain counts are summed"). The notation enables no proof or bound.

### Issues
- "D = ((A1), . . . , (Am)) where: Ai ... is a text": a list of strings in formal dress.
- "VWi = 1 for i = 1, . . . , K ... OWj = 0 for j = 1, . . . , N": initialising counters.
- Ck is computed as R(D) x PkT although R'(D) was just introduced for this purpose; V0 is defined with O+ instead of O0; the claim that the most competent voter gets Ck = [1, ..., 1] only holds with normalized weights.

---

## Citation Analysis

One self-citation of 17 references ([6] Stefan, Cyber-Physical Society - iDemocracy), directly on topic. SCR about 6%. The reference list is dominated by popular and self-published books, Kindle locations and web articles, with an opening epigraph; scholarly grounding on e-voting security or liquid democracy is thin, but this is not a self-citation problem.

---

## Structural Analysis

The paper is argumentative rather than empirical. Claims about society, markets, politicians and AI governance are stated as fact without evidence, and the proposed mechanism is never simulated or tested. A few limitations are noted inline (the iterative loop "is not always convergent"; iDemocracy "is not always a good solution provider"). Nothing is available to release.

---

## Conclusion

An opinion essay with a sketched voting scheme. The matrix and list notation adds an appearance of rigour to what is a weighted vote count, which triggers the zero-tolerance theater rule at Level 1, and the broader argument is largely unsupported.

paper.title: Peripheral Nerve WIFI Interfaces and Electrodes for Mechatronic Prosthetic Hand
paper.abstract: In this paper a unified approach of a nerve direct coupled electronic controller for hand prostheses is presented. The study starts with the forearm and hand dynamics analysis in order to achieve a neural interface connecting the peripheral median nerve from the patient's amputee arm with a prosthetic hand. After identifying the median and the ulnar nerves, the nerve direct coupling system is presented and the command electrodes experimental implantation in the operating amputee arm was performed. The proposed experimental system for the biopotentials generated by a motor nerve fiber using electrodes positioned on the nerve to control a hand prosthesis is shown. The peripheral interface is connected to a prosthetic hand with independent fingers in order to test the possibility of a nervous direct control for fingers motion.

artifact_assessment.evidence: no availability statement or link in the text; the interface schematics and PCB are only shown as figures, and the electrode is a commercial product ("Microelectrode Neurography Needle 30080 [6]")

flag_details.UNSUPPORTED_CLAIMS: The central result, that "the achieved signal from the median nerve can command the first three fingers using a special designed interface", is supported only by an unlabelled figure (Fig. 8); no signal amplitudes, SNR, classification rates or trial counts are reported for the single patient. The conclusion that "ethical problems, cognitive and emotional loads, were scientifically surmounted" has no supporting data.

verdict.summary: Descriptive report of an implanted nerve-electrode interface built from commercial components, with a single-patient trial reported without quantitative results; no formalism, but the claims of successful finger control are not substantiated.

paper.title: Mechatronic Finger Structure with Pressure-Sensitive Conductive Layer
paper.abstract: In this paper a unified approach of a mechatronic hand enriched with a pressure sensitive layer is analyzed. New developments of advanced applications regarding the Additive Manufacturing (AM) have been investigated and implemented. The analyze starts with a finger physical implementation, using 3-D printing technology. Digital Light Processing (DLP) is the 3-D printing selected process for finger structure manufacture. Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) is another additive process used for outer protective layer and for its mold manufacture. A pressure-sensitive layer of Velostat is inserted between the outer protective layer and the finger structure. The paper presents a simple and efficient prototype of a finger, using a cheap and sufficient accurate solution based on new materials. The finger manufacturing process begins with the design of three-dimensional model for the mold without any supplementary equipment and classic technologies. Starting from a finger mechanical structure with its three phalanges, it is developed by adding a pressure sensitive layer of Velostat, towards a future desired artificial skin. Its electrical properties recommend it as a first layer that covers the printed finger structure. Another outer protective layer is also added. This finger structure will be integrated in a designed hand system.

artifact_assessment.evidence: no availability statement or link in the text; the 3D models of the finger and mold are shown only as figures, and the slicing tools (Replicator G, Creation Workshop) are third-party

verdict.summary: Prototype report of a 3D-printed finger with a Velostat pressure layer; mostly a textbook description of FDM and DLP, with the sensor characterisation borrowed from a web thesis and the authors' own tests reported without data.

paper.title: Intelligent Optimization on Correlation Entropy Matter-element Model of Innovation and Reform Pilot Area
paper.abstract: In this paper, the correlation entropy matter element model, which is used to evaluate comprehensive competitiveness of innovation and reform pilot area, is Intelligent optimized. After analyzing the connotation of "regional strategy" of Chinese innovation evolutionary path, we build a comprehensive competitiveness evaluation system of the pilot area by combining internal relations and differences among the comprehensive innovation and reform pilot area, the national high-tech Development Zone, and the indigenous innovation demonstration zone. Through using composite correlation entropy matter-element model of grey correlation, this paper evaluates development of eight regions (those are Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, Sichuan, Anhui, Guangzhou, Shanghai, Wuhan, Xi'an, Shenyang etc.) from four dimensions of support vector ability, innovation ability, social contribution, export earning power, and comprehensive competitiveness of the eight regions is ranked. Finally, countermeasures and suggestions are proposed for advantages and shortcomings of the eight pilot zones.
keywords: comprehensive innovation and reform pilot area

artifact_assessment.evidence: "It depends on publication data from 'China Torch Statistical Yearbook 2015', 'China Statistical Yearbook of science and technology 2015', 'China Statistical Yearbook 2015' and regional data of official website, in which D6, D7, D8, D9, D10, D11 and other qualitative indicators originate from 'China City Competitiveness Report 2015'." No code (the Matlab 7.0 program) is released.

flag_details.FORMALISM_THEATER: Level 2 application of the standard entropy-weight / grey-relational scoring to eight regions. The data table and weight vector are dressed as 'composite matter-elements' (S, R~mn, Rwj, R~mH in Eqs. 1, 5, 8, 9), which are a labelled matrix and a labelled vector; the notation adds nothing a programmer would need and is itself inconsistent (it states "M=3, N=36" for eight zones).
flag_details.UNNECESSARY_SET_THEORY: Index types are introduced as sets "J+ ={benefit index}, J- ={cost index}, Jinterval ={interval index}" and used as j in J+ to select a normalisation formula; this is a per-column lookup of which of three formulas to apply, not set theory.

verdict.summary: Applies a standard entropy-weight grey-relational ranking to eight Chinese pilot zones; the data matrix is wrapped in matter-element and set notation, the method description contains errors, and no limitations are acknowledged.

## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** Ranking eight Chinese innovation pilot zones on a 36-indicator hierarchy using min-max normalisation, grey relational coefficients, entropy weights and a weighted entropy score.
**Level:** 2 (Low)
**Rationale:** Every step is a textbook multi-criteria evaluation method applied to a new set of regions; the paper's "intelligent optimization" is not described beyond these standard formulas.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 0 numbered
- Theorems: 0
- Proofs: 0
- Equations: 9 numbered (matter-element matrices, three normalisation formulas, grey coefficient, entropy, weights, composite score)

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 0
Expected range (Level 2): 0-15
Ratio: 0x upper bound

**Assessment:** The normalisation, grey-coefficient and entropy formulas are legitimate basic equations. The matter-element wrappers and the J+/J-/Jinterval sets fail the necessity test: they restate a data table and a column-type lookup.

### Issues
- "it is called N dimensional complex matter element of M pilot zones ... that is M=3, N=36" although eight zones are evaluated.
- Eq. (4) for interval indices is garbled and mixes u, v and mu.
- "The bigger the entropy is, the more information the index obtains" inverts the entropy-weight logic the method relies on (weights use 1 - F).
- Table 2 relabels the social-contribution sub-indices as D12-D15 instead of D23-D30, gives no weights for D31-D36, and the text states innovation capacity has weight 0.5314 while the table gives 0.2991.

---

## Citation Analysis

Co-author ShuHua Hu appears on three of 19 references ([12], [14], [16]), all on Chinese high-tech zones and demonstration zones and therefore topically related. SCR about 16%, in the elevated band. The in-text citation of Ahmed R. as [19] points to a Kangjuan Lv paper, and [18]/[19] appear swapped; [5] and [9] are the same paper cited twice.

---

## Structural Analysis

Input data come from named public statistical yearbooks, but the computed indicator values are not reported, so the ranking cannot be checked. Much of Section 4.2 consists of policy commentary unsupported by the model output. There is no limitations section and no acknowledgement of the sensitivity of entropy weights, the qualitative indicators, or the single-year data. Code is not released.

---

## Conclusion

A routine multi-criteria ranking presented with decorative matter-element and set notation, which triggers the Level 2 zero-tolerance rule. Errors in the method description and weight tables, and the absence of limitations, further weaken it.

paper.title: Study on Collaborative Control of Vehicle System at Road Intersection in Dynamic Competitive Environment
paper.abstract: By analyzing the conflict form of the road intersection, the time and space trajectory diagram was used to analyze the area where the vehicle may collide through the intersection. The vehicle coordination control model of the road intersection was established by using the safety index and the fastness index weighted processing. The model was used to construct the fitness function by using the penalty function method. The particle swarm optimization algorithm was used to solve the model, and the optimal acceleration of the vehicle was obtained.

artifact_assessment.evidence: no availability statement or link in the text; the Matlab implementation of the penalty-function PSO is not released

verdict.summary: Formulates intersection vehicle coordination as a weighted safety/time objective solved by standard penalty-function PSO on one six-vehicle example; equations are needed for the model but contain errors, and there is no validation or comparison.

papers.provenance:
## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** Choosing accelerations for vehicles approaching an unsignalised crossing by minimising a weighted sum of space-time trajectory overlap and passage time, subject to speed, acceleration and headway constraints, solved with standard particle swarm optimisation.
**Level:** 2 (Low)
**Rationale:** The objective is a straightforward weighted formulation and the solver is an off-the-shelf PSO with a quadratic penalty; there is no new algorithm or analysis.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 0
- Theorems: 0
- Proofs: 0
- Equations: 16 (kinematics, arc-length integrals, objective, constraints, penalty terms, PSO updates)

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 0
Expected range (Level 2): 0-15
Ratio: 0x upper bound

**Assessment:** Proportionate. The equations define the optimisation problem that is solved, so they pass the necessity test, though their quality is poor.

### Issues
Not theater, but several errors: the integration limits in Eqs. (2)-(5) (t_J3 to t_I2) and the statement that L is "less than zero" when there is no overlap; Eq. (11) gives the upper acceleration bound as a max with a_max instead of a min; t_r in Eq. (10) is inconsistent with Eq. (9); X'_I(t) = -A_I - a_I t uses A_I for speed where V_I was defined; Eq. (13) defines p but Eq. (14) uses P.

---

## Citation Analysis

Single author, seven references, no self-citations. Three references are off-topic for the points they support: [5] on yaw stability of brake-by-wire systems (cited for intersection force fields), [6] on a Matlab GUI sorting system (cited for computational convenience), and [7] on berth allocation (cited for the penalty method). The reference list is thin for the topic.

---

## Structural Analysis

The introduction claims the study is based on "specific operational experiments", but the only result is one set of six accelerations for a hand-picked example, with no check that the solution is collision-free, no sensitivity analysis and no comparison with the cited methods. The conclusion concedes that "a large number of cases to be verified", which counts as an inline limitation. Nothing is released.

---

## Conclusion

A weakly validated application of PSO to a simple intersection model. Formalism is proportionate to the problem, but the equations contain errors and the evidence is limited to one numerical example. The author name is printed as "HAN PENG"; following the journal's given-name-first order, Peng is taken as the surname.

paper.title: Analysis on Knowledge Innovation Efficiency of Agricultural Sci-tech Journal Community: Perspective of Knowledge Communication
paper.abstract: As a key content of the development of agricultural science and technology disciplines, the construction of the journal community has a strong practical significance in carrying out research on its knowledge innovation effectiveness. The effectiveness of knowledge innovation in the community of agricultural sci-tech journals was evaluated by using the non-parametric DEA-Tobit two-step model combined with the "Citation Report of Chinese Sci-tech Journals (Expanded Edition)", and the factors that affect the efficiency of the knowledge innovation in the journal community were argued. The conclusions are as follows: (1) Overall, the achievement of knowledge innovation in the community of agricultural sci-tech journals still has 34.4% of optimization space. The low efficiency of pure technology has a big impact. (2) There are large differences in the journal community, among which 12 journals have relatively stable knowledge innovation efficiency. (3) The academic quality of journal papers is an important factor in the efficiency of journal community knowledge innovation.

artifact_assessment.evidence: "the selection of research indicators mainly comes from the 2017 edition of 'China Science and Technology Journal Citation Report (Expanded Edition)'"; regional GDP "comes from the 'Statistical Bulletin of China National Economic and Social Development 2016'". No code or derived dataset is released (DEAP 2.1 and EViews 9.0 are third-party tools).

flag_details.NO_LIMITATIONS: No limitations section and no inline acknowledgement of constraints such as the single-year cross-section, the choice of DEA inputs and outputs, the known bias of second-stage Tobit regression on DEA scores, or the exclusion of 12 journals with missing data.

verdict.summary: Standard DEA-Tobit two-step efficiency study of 87 Chinese agricultural journals using public citation-report data; formalism is appropriate, but the conclusions overstate or contradict the regression table and no limitations are acknowledged.

papers.provenance:
## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** Input-oriented VRS DEA efficiency scores for 87 agricultural journals (2 inputs, 6 citation outputs), followed by Tobit regressions of the scores on seven journal and regional characteristics.
**Level:** 2 (Low)
**Rationale:** An established two-step econometric method applied to a new sample.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 0
- Theorems: 0
- Proofs: 0
- Equations: 2 (DEA linear program, Tobit model)

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 0
Expected range (Level 2): 0-15
Ratio: 0x upper bound

**Assessment:** Proportionate. The two models are stated in their standard form and are what is estimated.

### Issues
No theater, though the DEA program in Eq. (1) is garbled (the summations over lambda are missing from the constraints) and the text conflates N x 1 and M x 1 matrices with an undefined S. The Tobit error is given as N(0, delta^2) for both epsilon and Y*.

---

## Citation Analysis

No self-citations among 19 references. Reference [19] (neuro-fuzzy grey models for hot-rolling temperature prediction) is cited for the range of DEA efficiency scores and is unrelated; [18] on creative-industry parks is cited for the history of VRS DEA. These are weak citations but not self-citation problems.

---

## Structural Analysis

Descriptive tables and regression estimates are reported. However, the conclusions do not match Table 7: "duration of the publication" and regional GDP are called "positive factors" although neither is significant in Models 1 or 2; journal quality is called "an important factor" but is significant only for pure technical efficiency and negative for scale efficiency; the abstract says low pure technical efficiency has a big impact while the conclusion says "high efficiency". The number of journals published in Beijing is given as both 19 and 9. Table 7 carries the caption of Table 6. There is no limitations discussion. The data come from a named published citation report.

---

## Conclusion

A conventional application of DEA-Tobit with appropriate formalism. Its weaknesses are interpretive: several conclusions are not supported by the reported coefficients, and the study does not acknowledge any limitation.

paper.title: Analysis of Abnormal Crowd Movements based on Features Tracking
paper.abstract: Abnormal events in public places can be detected in real time by analyzing the video sequences from video posts, web or surveillance cameras. Sudden changes of speed and/or direction for all people moving in the scene may indicate the occurrence of an abnormal situation and in some conditions also the position in which the event occurred. The detection and tracking of the people in the scene require high computing resources which make this solution difficult to be applied for real time analysis especially in case of crowded scenes. In this paper is proposed an analyzer of scenes participants moving patterns. The Scale Invariant Features Transform (SIFT) is used for features extraction and the Lucas-Kanade (LK) algorithm for optical flow computation. The main advantage is that it requires low computing resources being suitable for real-time processing. The results obtained by applying the proposed method are compared to those obtained by other approaches presented in literature and also to the subjective evaluation of human observers.

artifact_assessment.evidence: "The experiment was conducted using 6 video sequences ... extracted from 'Crowd-Activity-All.avi' file available at 'Unusual crowd activity dataset' of University of Minnesota [34]"; [34] gives http://mha.cs.umn.edu. No code is linked.

verdict.summary: Applies SIFT matching and Lucas-Kanade optical flow with simple filtering and thresholding to detect abnormal crowd motion on six public UMN sequences; no formalism issues, a small but honest evaluation, and limitations acknowledged.

## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** Detecting abnormal crowd events by thresholding the filtered average displacement of SIFT features (compared with Lucas-Kanade optical flow) between consecutive frames.
**Level:** 2 (Low)
**Rationale:** Combines two standard computer-vision techniques with a minimum filter and a fixed threshold; an applied pipeline evaluated empirically.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 0
- Theorems: 0
- Proofs: 0
- Equations: 0

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 0
Expected range (Level 2): 0-15
Ratio: 0x upper bound

**Assessment:** Proportionate; the procedure is described in prose and a flowchart.

### Issues
None in formalism. The column headers of Table 3 omit the SIFT label for the second group of columns.

---

## Citation Analysis

Two self-citations among 35 references ([12] Luca on locomotion-type classification; [30] Bejinariu et al. on image registration, cited for SIFT details), both related. SCR about 6%. Three references by a colleague at the same institute ([25], [27], [28] Teodorescu) are on crowd and social-media event monitoring and are topically relevant.

---

## Structural Analysis

Results are reported per sequence as detected frame intervals and as sensitivity, specificity and accuracy against observer annotations, with some comparison to intervals reported in [7] and [8]. The thresholds were tuned on the same six sequences, which inflates the results, and the ground truth is acknowledged to be subjective. Limitations are stated inline: the small dataset, similar camera geometry, parameters needing retuning, and "work in progress". The dataset is public; code is not released.

---

## Conclusion

A modest, clearly reported applied study. Formalism and citations raise no concerns. The evaluation is small and tuned on the test data, but the authors say so.
